claim: Horizon placement decides whether a character dominates the sky or is crushed under the weight of the ground. Low horizon makes him a monument against open air; high horizon buries him in the pitch.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: no horizon visible, no sky in frame
very low horizon line, sky fills most of the frame
horizon on the lower third, sky above
horizon line through the center of the frame
horizon on the upper third, ground fills the lower frame
very high horizon line, ground fills most of the frame

review.issue: low ("very low horizon line, sky fills most of the frame") and lower_third ("horizon on the lower third, sky above") are the same instruction, as are high and upper_third — six options for about four pictures. And the fixed subject sentence puts the camera inside a floodlit stadium bowl surrounded by crowd, where the model rarely draws a horizon at all, so several panels risk silently becoming the none panel.
review.fix: Collapse to none / low / center / high. Note in the claim that the stadium location suppresses this variable, since that constraint is a property of the fixed subject sentence and worth stating before anyone reads the panels.

look_at: low and lower_third read; the upper half of the ladder does not.
